info.title: Travibe API
info.description:
# Travibe API

Welcome to the Travibe API — a simple REST API for authentication, user management, and account access.

## Quick Start

All API requests go to: **`/api/v1`**

For example: `https://travibe.com/api/v1/users`

## How to Authenticate

We use **token-based authentication**. Here's the flow:

1. **Sign up or log in** using the auth endpoints
2. **You'll get a token** in the response
3. **Add the token to your requests** in the `Authorization` header

```http
GET /api/v1/profile
Authorization: Bearer your_token_here
```

### Tokens

- Each device or app gets its own token
- Send a stable `device_name` with every auth request to label the session
- If you request a new token with the same `device_name`, you'll replace the old one
- Some endpoints (like changing your email) require a verified email address
- Tokens stay valid until you log out

## What You'll Get Back

### When it works

Successful responses contain your data wrapped in a `data` field:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "12345",
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "name": "John Doe"
  }
}
```

For operations that don't return data (like delete), you'll get a `204` status with an empty response.

### When something's wrong

**Validation errors** (status `422`):

```json
{
  "message": "Validation failed",
  "errors": {
    "email": ["Email is required", "Email must be valid"]
  }
}
```

**Other errors** (like bad credentials, status `401`):

```json
{
  "message": "Unauthorized"
}
```

## Limits & Pagination

- **Rate limiting:** You can make a reasonable number of requests per minute. If you hit the limit, you'll get a `429` status.
- **Pagination:** Use `page` and `per_page` query params on list endpoints:
  ```
  GET /api/v1/users?page=2&per_page=20
  ```

post.description:
Authenticates the account and returns a bearer access token scoped to the
supplied `device_name`. Requesting a token for an existing `device_name`
replaces that device's previous token, so each device keeps a single active session.
post.summary: Sign in with an email address and password

post.description:
Creates a new account and returns an access token. The token is restricted
until the account's email address is verified, and a verification email is
sent. Verify the email before calling endpoints that require a verified account.
post.summary: Create an account and start a device session

get.description:
Returns the profile of the authenticated user. Requires a bearer token
with full access and a verified email address.
get.summary: Get the authenticated user

post.description:
Revokes only the bearer token used for this request. Other device sessions
for the account remain active.

Returns the blocked user's public profile with refreshed follower and
following counts and `is_blocked: true`. Blocking yourself is a `422`.
Idempotent: blocking an already-blocked user returns `200` with the same
body and creates no duplicate.

A block is symmetric for interactions: after it, the pair can no longer
follow, like, comment on, save or share each other's content, and both
sides' posts are excluded from each other's feeds, profiles and saved
lists. Existing follows are left in place — unblock, then unfollow, to
clear both.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

get.description:
Returns the boolean plus the `user_id` it was computed for, which is
cheaper than paging through the blocked list when a screen only needs the
button state. This reports only your own block; a block by the other user
suppresses interaction too, but is not visible here.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.
get.summary: Check whether you have blocked a user

post.description:
Returns the user's public profile with refreshed follower and following
counts and `is_blocked: false`. Unblocking yourself is a `422`.
Idempotent: unblocking a user who is not blocked is a no-op.

Unblocking restores visibility both ways, but does not restore the
follows, likes and comments that were blocked while the block stood.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

get.description:
Returns public profiles, most recently blocked first, each with follower
and following counts and `is_following`, so the client can show whether an
unblock also needs an unfollow.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.
get.summary: List the users you have blocked

get.description:
Returns top-level comments newest first, each with its author, media,
reply count, like count and the viewer's own like state. Pass
`parent_id` to list the replies to one comment instead. Deleted comments
are never returned, and the post's `visibility` must allow the viewer
(otherwise `403`).

A bearer token is optional; sending an invalid or expired one returns
`401`.
get.summary: List a post's comments

per_page.description: Number of items shown per page.

post.description:
Requires `content`, `media_ids`, or both — an empty comment is a `422`.
`media_ids` must reference media the caller already presigned and
finalized. Pass `parent_id` to reply to another comment on the same post;
a parent that does not belong to this post is a `422`. Commenting is
rejected with `422` when the post has comments disabled or when either
party is in a block relationship.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

get.description:
The parent post's `visibility` must allow the viewer, otherwise `403`.
A deleted comment returns `404`, because the nested route binding ignores
soft-deleted comments.

A bearer token is optional; sending an invalid or expired one returns
`401`.
get.summary: Get a single comment

put.description:
Only the comment's author may edit it; anyone else gets a `403`. `content`
and `media_ids` are both optional — omitted fields keep their current
value, and supplied `media_ids` are added to the comment.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

delete.description:
Only the comment's author may delete it; anyone else gets a `403`.
Deleting is a soft delete, so the comment can be brought back with
`POST /posts/{post}/comments/{comment}/restore`. Its likes are removed
outright, and a reply's own replies are soft-deleted alongside it, so
they can only be restored individually. The post's comment count — and
the parent's reply count, for a reply — go down accordingly.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

post.description:
Brings back a soft-deleted comment owned by the caller and re-increments
the post's comment count (and the parent's reply count, for a reply).
Only the comment's author may restore it; anyone else gets a `403`. A
comment that is not currently deleted returns `404`.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

Marks the account verified and grants the caller's device token full
abilities when the token belongs to the verified account. A wrong or
expired code returns a 422 with one generic message, whether or not a
code is actually pending for the address. After five wrong attempts the
code is invalidated and a new one must be requested.
post.summary: Verify an email address with a 4-digit OTP code

post.description:
Public entry point for the "Didn't get OTP? Resend" flow. Throttling is
identity-blind: a 60-second cooldown and a 20-codes-per-day cap advance
whether or not the address has an account (or a verified one), so the
response never reveals account state. The echoed `email` is masked.

get.description:
Returns posts from everyone the authenticated user follows, plus the
user's own posts, newest first. Posts that are no longer active, that the
viewer has hidden, and posts written by (or quoting) a user in a block
relationship with the viewer are all excluded — blocking applies in both
directions. Visibility is respected, so `followers` posts only appear
once the viewer actually follows the author.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.
get.summary: List the posts that make up the following timeline

get.description:
Returns every active public post from every user, newest first, with the
viewer's own like and save state attached. Posts the viewer has hidden
and posts from users in a block relationship are excluded. Use
`GET /posts?user_id=` for a single author's posts — hiding does not apply
to author listings, only to feeds.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.
get.summary: List the public posts that make up the explore feed

post.description:
Returns the followed user's public profile with refreshed follower and
following counts and `is_following: true`, so the client can render the
button without a refetch. Following yourself is a `422`, following
someone you already follow is a `409`, and following a user in a block
relationship — in either direction — is a `422`.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

Returns the user's public profile with refreshed follower and following
counts and `is_following: false`. Unfollowing yourself is a `422`, and
unfollowing someone you do not follow is a `409`.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

get.description:
Returns the boolean plus the `user_id` it was computed for, which is
cheaper than paging through followers when a screen only needs the
button state. Always `false` for your own account.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.
get.summary: Check whether you follow a user

get.description:
Returns public profiles the viewer does not already follow, ordered by
follower count, with each entry's follower and following counts and
`is_following: false`. Users in a block relationship with the viewer and
the viewer themselves are never suggested.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.
get.summary: List users worth following

post.description:
Returns the resulting hidden state so the client can dismiss the post
without a refetch. Hiding is feed-only: it removes the post from
`GET /feed/explore` and `GET /feed/following` for this user and nobody
else. The post is still there for everyone else, still shows on its
author's profile and in `GET /posts?user_id=`, and is unaffected for the
author.

You cannot hide your own post — that is a `403`; use
`DELETE /posts/{post}` instead. Hiding is idempotent, and a post whose
`visibility` the viewer cannot see is a `403` as well.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.
post.summary: Hide a post from your feeds

delete.description:
Brings the post back into this user's explore and following feeds and
returns the resulting hidden state. Idempotent: unhiding a post that is
not hidden is a no-op. A post whose `visibility` the viewer cannot see is
a `403`.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

get.description:
Returns public profiles only, most recent like first, each with follower
and following counts and whether the viewer follows them. Users in a
block relationship with the viewer are omitted. The post's `visibility`
must allow the viewer, otherwise `403`.

A bearer token is optional; sending an invalid or expired one returns
`401`.
get.summary: List the users who liked a post

per_page.description: Number of items shown per page.

get.description:
Returns public profiles only, most recent like first, each with follower
and following counts and whether the viewer follows them. Users in a
block relationship with the viewer are omitted. The parent post's
`visibility` must allow the viewer, otherwise `403`.

A bearer token is optional; sending an invalid or expired one returns

get.summary: List the users who liked a comment

path.description: Base path for paginator generated URLs.

per_page.description: Number of items shown per page.

to.description: Number of the last item in the slice.

total.description: Total number of items being paginated.

post.description:
Returns the resulting like state and the post's updated like count so
the client never has to refetch the post. Idempotent: liking an
already-liked post returns `is_liked: true` with the same count and does
not create a duplicate. Liking content from a user in a block
relationship — in either direction — is a `422`.

The post's `visibility` must allow the viewer, otherwise `403`.
Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

delete.description:
Returns the resulting like state and the post's updated like count.
Idempotent: unliking a post that is not liked is a no-op. The post's
`visibility` must allow the viewer, otherwise `403`.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.
delete.summary: Remove your like from a post

post.description:
Returns the resulting like state and the comment's updated like count.
Idempotent, and rejected with `422` for content from a user in a block
relationship. The parent post's `visibility` must allow the viewer,
otherwise `403`.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

delete.description:
Returns the resulting like state and the comment's updated like count.
Idempotent: unliking a comment that is not liked is a no-op. The parent
post's `visibility` must allow the viewer, otherwise `403`.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.
delete.summary: Remove your like from a comment

post.description:
The client uploads the bytes directly to object storage, then calls
finalize. Send `filename`, `content_type` (must be one of the allowed
image MIME types) and `size`; a size over the configured per-type maximum
is a `422` here rather than at upload time. Optional `mediable_type` and
`mediable_id` pre-declare the post or comment the media will belong to.

Upload with the returned `upload_method` (`PUT`) to `upload_url`, sending
every header in `upload_headers` exactly as given — they are part of the
signature, and a mismatch is rejected by storage. The URL expires at
`expires_at` (10 minutes by default); after that, presign again.

The record starts at `status: pending`. The declared `content_type` is
not yet trusted — finalize verifies what actually landed in storage. Pass
the returned `media.id` to `POST /posts`, `PUT /posts/{post}` or a
comment request to claim it.

No email verification required.
post.summary: Request a presigned upload URL and create a pending Media record

post.description:
Moves the record from `pending` to `processing` and queues the async job
that produces the derived sizes; poll `GET /media/{media}` for `ready` or
`failed`. A presigned URL is not validation — the stored object is
measured and its real content type is sniffed, so an oversized or
unsupported upload is rejected with `422` and the record goes to `failed`.
An upload that never arrived is also a `422`. Calling finalize twice, or
racing two calls, gives `409` — only the first caller dispatches the job.

Only the media's owner may finalize it; anyone else gets a `403`.
No email verification required.
post.summary: Verify the uploaded object and dispatch async processing

get.description:
Returns `status` as `pending`, `processing`, `ready` or `failed`, plus the
declared type, verified MIME type, byte `size`, `width`/`height` and the
`url` and `thumbnail_url` once processing has produced them. A failed
record also carries an `error`, and `mediable_type`/`mediable_id` show
which post or comment the media has been claimed by.

Visible to the owner of the media and to any authenticated user for
ownerless records; anyone else gets a `403`. No email verification
required.
get.summary: Show the current media record and processing status

get.description:
Returns the slides shown on the first-launch screens (`key`, `title`,
`body`, `asset_url`) in `sort_order` order. Content is managed from the
admin panel, not hardcoded. Cached for 24 hours; edits reflect
immediately; responses carry `ETag` + `Cache-Control` for HTTP caching.
get.summary: List the active onboarding slides

get.description:
Backs the language picker: the two-letter `code`, a display `name` and
an `rtl` flag per locale, plus the `default`. No authentication.
get.summary: List the supported app locales

post.description:
Sends a 4-digit reset code to the account matching the email address.
For security, the response is identical whether or not the address
exists.

Verifies the 4-digit code sent by the forgot-password flow and returns a
short-lived reset token for `POST /reset-password`. Codes expire after
ten minutes and allow five attempts before a new one must be requested.
A wrong or expired code returns a 422 with one generic message, whether
or not a code is actually pending for the address.
post.summary: Exchange a reset code for a password reset token

post.description:
Completes the password reset with the token and email from the code
exchange. The `password` and `password_confirmation` fields must match.
On success every existing device session is revoked, so all devices must
sign in again with the new password.
post.summary: Set a new password using a reset token

get.description:
Without `user_id` this is the explore feed (see `GET /feed/explore`).
With `user_id` it becomes an author's post list: visibility-filtered for
the viewer and block-filtered, but deliberately *not* hidden-filtered, so
a hidden post still shows on its author's profile. A blocked author — in
either direction — returns an empty page rather than an error.

A bearer token is optional: it only decides whether `followers`-only posts
and the viewer's like/save state are included. Send an invalid or expired
token and the request fails with `401`.
get.summary: Explore feed, or a single author's posts when `?user_id=` is present

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Show only this author's posts. Omit for the explore feed.

path.description: Base path for paginator generated URLs.

per_page.description: Number of items shown per page.

to.description: Number of the last item in the slice.

total.description: Total number of items being paginated.

post.description:
Requires `content`, `media_ids`, or both — an empty post is a `422`.
`media_ids` must reference media the caller already presigned and
finalized; the media is claimed by this post. `visibility` defaults to
`public` and also accepts `followers` and `private`.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

get.description:
Returns the post with the viewer's like and save state plus its comment,
like and share counts. The post's `visibility` must allow the viewer:
`public` for anyone, `followers` for the author and their followers,
`private` for the author alone. Anything else returns `403`, and a
soft-deleted post returns `404`.

A bearer token is optional; sending an invalid or expired one returns
`401`.
get.summary: Get a single post

put.description:
Only the author may update their own post; anyone else gets a `403`.
Every field is optional: omitted fields keep their current value, and
supplied `media_ids` are added to the post. Editing a repost or quote is
allowed but forced back to `public` visibility — clearing `content` turns
a quote into a repost, adding content turns a repost into a quote.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

delete.description:
Only the author may delete their own post; anyone else gets a `403`.
Deleting is a soft delete, so the post disappears from feeds and from
`GET /posts/{post}` but can be brought back with `POST /posts/{post}/restore`
within the soft-delete window. Deleting a post also permanently removes
its comments, likes, shares, saves and hides.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

post.description:
Brings back a soft-deleted post owned by the caller and recomputes its
comment, like and share counts. Only the author may restore; anyone else
gets a `403`. A post that is not currently deleted is treated as missing
and returns `404`.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

get.description:
Backs the live check while typing: returns the normalized `username`
and `available`. Validation failures (shape rules) return 422.
get.summary: Check whether a username is available

patch.description:
Accepts any subset of: `full_name` (or legacy `name`), `username`
(nullable clears it), `country_code` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2),
`avatar_media_id` (the user's own media, `Ready` or `Processing`),
`languages_spoken` (max 4), `interests` (max 6) and `travel_styles`
(max 3). Sync is idempotent, so repeating a step overwrites prior
values. Clearing a required selection un-completes a finished profile.
Every response echoes the next wizard step and completion state.

post.description:
Requires `full_name`, `username`, 1–4 languages, 1–6 interests and
1–3 travel styles — a 422 lists every missing requirement at once.
On success sets `profile_completed_at` and returns the user with
`meta.profile_completed: true`. Skipping stays allowed; completion can
happen later without any penalty.

get.description:
Returns active languages as `{slug, name, name_en, name_ar, status}`.
Optional `?search=` matches slug or either localized name. `name` is
localized per `Accept-Language`; cached for 24 hours.
get.summary: List languages available for profile setup

post.description:
Creates a language with `status: pending` or returns the existing match
(then and on concurrent creation: 200 with that language; new creation:
201). Pending languages can only be attached to a profile by the user
who requested them until an admin approves them to `active`.
post.summary: Request a custom language for the profile-setup wizard

get.description:
Returns `{slug, name, name_en, name_ar}`. `name` is localized per
`Accept-Language`; cached for 24 hours.
get.summary: List interests available for profile setup

get.description:
Returns `{slug, name, name_en, name_ar}`. `name` is localized per
`Accept-Language`; cached for 24 hours.
get.summary: List travel styles available for profile setup

post.description:
`type` is `post`, `comment` or `user`, and `id` is that target's ID.
`reason` is one of `spam_or_scam`, `harassment`,
`inappropriate_content` or `something_else`; `description` is an
optional free-text note of up to 1000 characters.

You can only report content you are allowed to see — a target hidden
from you by visibility or a block is reported as "does not exist"
(`422`), and you cannot report yourself. One pending report per target
per reporter is allowed; filing a second one while the first is still
pending is a `422`. Reports start as `pending` for moderation review;
this endpoint does not remove the reported content.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.
post.summary: Report a post, comment or user

post.description:
Returns the resulting save state so the client can flip the bookmark
without a refetch. Idempotent: saving an already-saved post returns
`is_saved: true` and does not create a duplicate. The post's
`visibility` must allow the viewer (otherwise `403`), and saving a post
from a user in a block relationship is a `422`.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

delete.description:
Returns the resulting save state. Idempotent: unsaving a post that is
not saved is a no-op. The post's `visibility` must still allow the
viewer, otherwise `403`.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.
delete.summary: Remove a post from your saved list

get.description:
Returns the caller's saved posts, most recently saved first, with the
viewer's like state attached. The list is visibility-filtered and
block-filtered — a saved post disappears once it is deleted or once
either party is in a block relationship. Hiding a post does not affect
the saved list.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.
get.summary: List your saved posts

get.description:
Returns each share with its public author, the platform it was shared
on and any accompanying comment, newest first. The post's `visibility`
must allow the viewer, otherwise `403`.

A bearer token is optional; sending an invalid or expired one returns
`401`.
get.summary: List who shared a post

path.description: Base path for paginator generated URLs.

per_page.description: Number of items shown per page.

to.description: Number of the last item in the slice.

total.description: Total number of items being paginated.

post.description:
Only `public` posts can be shared; anything else is a `422`. `platform`
defaults to `internal` and also accepts `facebook`, `twitter`, `linkedin`,
`whatsapp`, `email` and `copy_link`; `comment` is an optional note of up
to 500 characters. Sharing the same post twice is a `422`, as is sharing
a post from a user in a block relationship.

An `internal` share additionally creates a repost (or a quote, when
`comment` is present) on the caller's profile and increments the post's
share count; the other platforms only record the share.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

delete.description:
Only the share's author may remove it; anyone else gets a `403`. Removing
an `internal` share also deletes the repost or quote it created, and the
post's share count goes down. Removing a share does not delete the
original post.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

post.description:
Exchanges a provider identity token for a Travibe bearer token. The
identity token must come from the provider's native or web sign-in flow.
Apple sign-ins require the original `nonce`, which is accepted only once.
A new token for an existing `device_name` replaces that device's previous token.
post.summary: Exchange a Google or Apple identity token for a bearer token

get.description:
Returns the authenticated user's active tokens (device sessions). Token
values are never returned; the session used for the current request is
flagged with `current: true`. Requires a bearer token with full access
and a verified email address.
get.summary: List active device sessions

delete.description:
Revokes a single token owned by the authenticated user. The token used for
this request can also be revoked. Returns `404` when the token does not
belong to the user. Requires a bearer token with full access and a
verified email address.

ForgotPasswordRequest.description:
Body for requesting a password reset code.

The V1 contract currently matches Fortify's validated email payload, so this
adds only a docblock over the inherited rules.
ForgotPasswordRequest.title: ForgotPasswordRequest

LanguageRequest.description: Body for requesting a custom language during profile setup.

name.description:
The language's display name, e.g. "Cantonese". Letters, spaces
and hyphens only; 2-50 characters. Creates a `pending` language
that only the requesting user can attach until an admin approves it.

LanguageRequest.title: LanguageRequest

LoginRequest.description: Body for signing in with an email address and password.

device_name.description:
A label for this device session, e.g. the device model. Reusing
a name replaces that device's previous token.

LoginRequest.title: LoginRequest

PresignMediaRequest.description:
Body for requesting a presigned upload URL.

Uploads currently accept images only.

filename.description: The file's original name. Max 255 characters.

content_type.description:
The file's MIME type. Must be one of the allowed image types.
Untrusted — finalize verifies what actually landed in storage.

size.description:
The file's size in bytes. Rejected here if over the per-type
maximum (20 MB by default).

mediable_type.description: Optional model class the media will belong to, e.g. `App\Models\Post`.

mediable_id.description:
Optional ID of the record the media will belong to. Required
whenever `mediable_type` is sent.

PresignMediaRequest.title: PresignMediaRequest

ProfileSetupRequest.description:
Body for updating the profile-setup wizard.

Every field is optional; only the sent fields change. Slug arrays are
synced, so repeating a step overwrites the previous selection.

full_name.description:
The profile's display name. Max 255 characters. `name` is
accepted as a legacy alias.

username.description:
The `@`-less handle. 3-30 characters of letters, digits,
underscores or dots, and unique across accounts. Send `null` to
clear it; clearing after completing profile setup un-completes it.

avatar_media_id.description:
The caller's own media to use as the avatar. Accepts media in
`ready` or `processing` status so the wizard need not wait for
async conversion. Send `null` to clear.

languages_spoken.description: Language slugs the user speaks. 1-4 entries; send `null` to clear.

items.description:
Active languages are available to everyone; a pending custom
submission can only be attached by the user who requested it.

interests.description: Interest slugs, e.g. `food`. 1-6 entries; send `null` to clear.

travel_styles.description: Travel style slugs, e.g. `budget`. 1-3 entries; send `null` to clear.

ProfileSetupRequest.title: ProfileSetupRequest

RegisterRequest.description: Body for creating an account and a device session.

email.description:
The account's email address. Must not already be registered.
A verification code is sent here on success.

password.description:
The account password. Must satisfy the configured complexity
rules and be confirmed by `password_confirmation`.

device_name.description:
A label for this device session, e.g. the device model. Reusing
a name replaces that device's previous token.

terms_accepted.description:
Must be `true` — the caller has accepted the terms and privacy
policy.

RegisterRequest.title: RegisterRequest

ResendOtpRequest.description:
Body for resending a verification code.

The response is the same whether or not the address has an account.

email.description: The email address to send the code to.

ResendOtpRequest.title: ResendOtpRequest

ResetPasswordRequest.description: Body for completing a password reset with a reset token.

token.description: The short-lived reset token from the code exchange.

email.description: The account's email address, matching the one the code was sent to.

password.description:
The new password. Must satisfy the configured complexity rules
and be confirmed by `password_confirmation`.

ResetPasswordRequest.title: ResetPasswordRequest

SocialAuthTokenRequest.description: Body for exchanging a provider identity token for a Travibe bearer token.

device_name.description:
A label for this device session, e.g. the device model. Reusing
a name replaces that device's previous token.

id_token.description:
The identity token issued by Google or Apple by its own sign-in
flow. Max 10000 characters.

nonce.description:
The `nonce` sent to Apple at sign-in. Required for `apple`, and
accepted only once.

name.description:
The account's display name, used only when the provider does not
supply one for a first-time signup.

SocialAuthTokenRequest.title: SocialAuthTokenRequest

StoreCommentRequest.description:
Body for creating or editing a comment.

A comment must carry content, media, or both.

media_ids.description: IDs of media the caller has presigned and finalized.

parent_id.description:
Reply to this comment instead of posting at the top level. Must
be a comment on the same post.

StoreCommentRequest.title: StoreCommentRequest

StorePostRequest.description:
Body for creating a post.

A post must carry content, media, or both.

media_ids.description:
IDs of media the caller has presigned and finalized. Required
when `content` is empty; each ID must already belong to the
caller.

anyOf.description:
Who can see the post. `public`, `followers` or `private`.
Defaults to `public`.

StorePostRequest.title: StorePostRequest

StoreReportRequest.description: Body for filing a report against a post, comment or user.

id.description: The ID of the reported post, comment or user.

reason.description:
Why it is being reported: `spam_or_scam`, `harassment`,
`inappropriate_content` or `something_else`.

StoreReportRequest.title: StoreReportRequest

StoreShareRequest.description:
Body for sharing a post.

Both fields are optional; sharing without them records an internal share.

anyOf.description:
Where the post was shared: `internal`, `facebook`, `twitter`,
`linkedin`, `whatsapp`, `email` or `copy_link`. Defaults to
`internal`. An `internal` share also creates a repost, or a
quote when `comment` is present.

comment.description:
Optional note to attach to the share. Max 500 characters. On an
`internal` share this becomes the repost or quote text.

StoreShareRequest.title: StoreShareRequest

UpdatePostRequest.description:
Body for updating a post.

Every field is optional; omitted fields keep their current value.

content.description:
The post text. Max 2000 characters. Ignored for reposts and
quotes, which are forced back to `public` visibility.

media_ids.description: IDs of media to add to the post. Existing media is kept.

anyOf.description: Who can see the post. `public`, `followers` or `private`.

comments_disabled.description:
Whether new comments are rejected on this post. Existing
comments are kept either way.

UpdatePostRequest.title: UpdatePostRequest

VerifyOtpRequest.description:
Body for exchanging a 4-digit code for a token.

Used by both the email-verification and password-reset flows; which one is
determined by the endpoint, not by this payload.

email.description: The email address the code was sent to.

VerifyOtpRequest.title: VerifyOtpRequest

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.
